lanes.evidence: Satellite: two curved left-turn arrows inside the r1 outline (near the stop bar and about mid-panel). C1 look-back: a large left-turn arrow in the lane on the right of the photo (driver's left = r1) with the word ONLY just upstream of it; C2 forward also shows ONLY in the left lane r1. Lane lines and stop bar reach it; vehicles drive in it. Left-only lane next to the median.

Satellite: two straight-ahead arrows in the r2 outline aligned with the r1 left arrows. C1 look-back: a large straight arrow pointing toward the junction in the lane left of the photo centre (driver's right general lane = r2). r2 is the curbside general motor lane, but the junction has no exit on the driver's right (north-east side is a building and a park in the overview), so no right turn is available; the bicycle lane between r2 and the curb is not a motor lane.

movements.reason: Left arrows and ONLY in r1; Ames Street leg to the south-west is the only left exit (out_SB, -91 deg).
Straight arrows in r2; Broadway continues north-west as out_WB.
T-junction: no road leaves to the driver's right (north-east), the overview shows a building and park there and no right exit is listed.
No U-turn arrow or sign seen; r1 shows plain left-turn arrows only. A U-turn around the median into out_EB is not evidenced.

temporary_control.evidence: No cones, barrels or work-zone devices on the approach lanes in the satellite or in C1-C3.

notes: Approach widens from one lane upstream (C3) to two lanes near the junction: r1 left-only, r2 through. The curbside strip right of r2 is a bicycle lane behind a solid white line (bicycle symbol visible in C1); it is not counted as a motor lane, and it does not matter for turns because no right exit exists. Satellite date unknown; street views 2020-11.
